detail.longDescription: Security researchers at NebuSec have disclosed a sandbox escape vulnerability chain affecting Meta's Muse AI agent, demonstrating how a malicious webpage could lead to root access on the agent's underlying cloud VM. The attack began when Muse was instructed to save an attacker-controlled webpage as a PDF. Researchers exploited a Chromium vulnerability to achieve code execution inside the browser container, bypassed network restrictions to exfiltrate data and chained a Linux kernel vulnerability to gain root privileges on the user VM. The resulting access potentially exposed sensitive information, including private conversations, stored memories and credentials. Researchers also demonstrated the ability to modify the agent's conversation history and persistent memories, raising concerns about the integrity of future AI interactions. Importantly, the exploit did not compromise the hypervisor or other customers' virtual machines. Testing was conducted within the researchers' own environment, and NebuSec reports that Meta patched the identified weaknesses before public disclosure. The research highlights how multiple security boundaries can fail when AI agents process untrusted web content with access to sensitive user data and privileged execution environments. Full technical analysis and exploit chain: https:// thecybersecguru.com/exploits/m eta-muse-sandbox-escape-nebusec/ # AIAgents # SandboxEscape # Meta # CyberSecurity
